label: an approximate reconstruction from the cited claims, not the experiment's geometry
subsystem: RICH1 (C4F10) and RICH2 (CF4) gas radiators, Upgrade I

quantities.name: cherenkov_angle_c4f10
quantities.definition: mean Cherenkov angle (rad) of the photons a 100 GeV (kinetic) muon emits in the RICH1 C4F10 radiator, detected inside the gas; per-event mean, averaged over events
quantities.derivation: arccos(1/(n beta)) with n = 1.0014 at 400 nm and STP (detector-atlas:C154; 0 C and 101.325 kPa, C156) and beta = 0.99999944 for T = 100000 MeV and the muon mass 105.6583755 MeV (core/constants, CODATA 2022): 0.0528737 rad (0.0528842 at beta = 1). Tolerance 2%: n printed to 1e-4 moves the angle by -1.80% / +1.77% for n -+ 0.00005.

independence.result: independent of Geant4: a closed form of the index LHCb states at 400 nm and the muon kinematics; no simulation enters the reference (the simulated resolutions and photoelectron yields of the Upgrade I paper's table 9 are not used). Geant4 samples the same relation, so agreement validates the optical material, the photon accounting and the reading of the angle, not Cherenkov physics.

quantities.name: cherenkov_angle_cf4
quantities.definition: mean Cherenkov angle (rad) of the photons a 100 GeV (kinetic) muon emits in the RICH2 CF4 radiator, detected inside the gas; per-event mean, averaged over events
quantities.derivation: arccos(1/(n beta)) with n = 1.0005 at 400 nm and STP (detector-atlas:C155, C156) and beta = 0.99999944 as above: 0.0315986 rad (0.0316162 at beta = 1). Tolerance 5.2%: n printed to 1e-4 moves the angle by -5.14% / +4.88% for n -+ 0.00005.

independence.result: independent of Geant4: a closed form of the index LHCb states at 400 nm and the muon kinematics; no simulation enters the reference (the simulated resolutions and photoelectron yields of the Upgrade I paper's table 9 are not used). Geant4 samples the same relation, so agreement validates the optical material, the photon accounting and the reading of the angle, not Cherenkov physics.

approximations: each radiator is a 400 x 400 mm2 box of gas whose length is the stated average path in it (110 cm for RICH1, approximately; 167 cm for RICH2; C154, C155), not the RICH enclosures, mirrors, windows or photon detectors
the index is constant over 390-410 nm at its 400 nm value: the dispersion is not sourced
pure CF4: the Run 1 radiator had about 5% CO2 (C156) and the Upgrade I admixture is not stated; pure C4F10
gas densities from the ideal-gas law at 0 C and 101.325 kPa (C156) with stoichiometric molar masses; the angle does not depend on them

the world has no refractive index, so a photon reaching a radiator face is absorbed; the 300 x 300 x 1 mm3 silicon sensor 1 mm inside the downstream face (efficiency 1, reflectivity 0) is a measuring device, not LHCb's MaPMTs

cherenkov_handling.label: (a)
cherenkov_handling.scintillation: none: the gases carry no scintillation yield, so no efficiency map is needed
cherenkov_handling.note: every Cherenkov photon is tracked; the angle is read from the photons the primary emitted (parent track 1)

status: comparison with cited values: not validated
